raw_response:
I am 58 years old and I have farmed this 10.9 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished middle school, so I can read fertilizer labels and calculate costs, but I still trust what I see in my own field more than anything a salesman tells me. Last year my 7 mu of wheat gave me about 530 jin per mu and my 3.9 mu of cotton gave me about 500 jin per mu, so I will stick with almost the same plan this year because changing things is risky.

For wheat, I sow the improved Shannong variety in October. I spread one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base, which costs me about 140 yuan per bag, and I top-dress with 20 kg of urea per mu at jointing. I irrigate three times from my well: overwintering, jointing, and grain-filling. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once, so two pesticide applications. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the spring weather is normal.

After the wheat comes off in early June, I plant hybrid Zhengdan 958 maize on that same 7 mu. I use no-tillage direct seeding to save labor and diesel. I put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting and 20 kg of urea per mu when the plants are knee-high. I will irrigate twice: once after planting if the soil is dry, and once at the filling stage. Two pesticide sprays: one for weeds and one for corn borer. I expect about 650 kg per mu.

My 3.9 mu cotton field is different. Cotton needs loose soil, so I plough it in April. I put one 50 kg bag of compound per mu plus 10 kg of potassium chloride because cotton needs more potassium. When it flowers I top-dress with 25 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: seedling, flowering, and boll stage. Cotton pests are bad here, especially bollworm, so I spray five times. I use the improved Bt cotton seed. I hope for 260 kg of seed cotton per mu. I know fertilizer is expensive—one bag of compound is almost 150 yuan now—but I would rather spend the money than risk a bad harvest. A failed crop means my family loses thousands of yuan; wasting half a bag of fertilizer only costs a few dozen yuan. I watch what my neighbors do, and most of them around here use about the same amounts, so I do the same.
